_comment: The tower: a hoodoo column with a hollow watch chamber cut into its top. ORIGIN IS THE ROOM'S FLOOR -- the guard stands at local y=0 and TowerSpawn lands 0.25 m above it; the rock hangs down to y=-36.4 and the drum's top is at +9.6. One textured material (128x128 atlas + emissive), one UV set, no skin, no animation. TowerCollision is the purpose-built collider that rides in the .glb as a `-colonly` node: Godot turns it into a StaticBody3D + ConcavePolygonShape3D and discards its mesh, which is why `surfaces` is still 1 and `max_tris` counts only what is drawn. If TowerCollision ever stops appearing, the model has silently gone back to having no collision at all and the guard will fall through the floor -- that is what these two node paths are here to catch.
